CHART OF THE DAY: Lots of noise today about European nat gas storage levels. I liked this chart from Greek deputy energy minister Nikos Tsafos (@ntsafos https://t.co/GDMcXxjYhx). While the Strait of Hormuz remains in crisis (but not fully closed), the rest of the world isn't still. Brazil is a great example. 

Brazilian oil production rose in June to an all-time high of nearly 4.5m b.d, up >700,000 b/d from June 2025 (and >1m b/d from June 2024).

Iraq is offering effectively a $25-$29 a barrel payment to anyone willing to risk loading at its port inside the Persian Gulf and take the barrels out.

On a single VLCC, that’s a ~$50-$58 million potential profit, minus costs (and the risk of getting sunk by Iran, that’s it).

Iran Foreign Ministry spokesperson on the Strait of Hormuz:

"Our negotiations are with Oman, we are focused on reaching an understanding on a route that will ensure safe shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Our effort is to determine a route at the earliest opportunity, with Oman's consultation and cooperation; a route that will usually be temporary and based on which we can provide shipping in the Strait of Hormuz..."

"So, these are bilateral negotiations between the two coastal states. Others can play a constructive or destructive role in this process, but the issue is with Iran and Oman. What happens next needs to be decided. I also announced last night that an understanding on the safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz is a necessary condition for the opening of Hormuz, but it is not a sufficient condition. The Strait of Hormuz is not closed because of a disagreement between Iran and Oman; Hormuz has been in trouble since March of last year due to the military aggression of the United States and the Zionist regime..."

"As long as America's evil continues, as long as the naval blockade of Iran is declared, as long as America's military aggression against Iran and its interests continues, and as long as all the things that America has violated during this period continue, there will be no significant change in the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Therefore, the focus of the negotiations with Oman will be on this issue, and the issues related to Iran and the United States should be examined in the next stages to see in which direction the situation will go..."

Despite all the "closed" talk about the Strait of Hormuz, a lot of oil keeps leaking, and the number of STS operations in the Gulf of Oman has climbed. All counted, probably ~5m b/d is flowing dark via SoH. Another reason why the physical market has weakened. https://t.co/mqKsavGeAv

Oil rally fades as belligerents back away from escalation

Investors made relatively few changes to their positions in crude oil and refined products last week as the conflict between the United States and Iran remained poised between further escalation and renewed negotiations.

The aggressive short-covering rally in Brent crude futures that characterised the two previous weeks ended as investors remained uncertain about whether sufficient crude could still be sent through the Strait of Hormuz.

There was even more uncertainty whether oil could be re-routed through the Red Sea following threats from Yemen’s Houthi militia against tankers transiting the Bab el-Mandeb at the southern end of the waterway ...

Oil exports from #Venezuela plunged in July due to weaker demand from India after a pause in the Iran war unlocked Middle Eastern barrels trapped in the Persian Gulf.

Venezuelan ship loadings of crude fell to a five-month low of 856,000 barrels a day last month, down 25% from June as shipments to India fell by half, according to shipping reports, data from Kpler Ltd, and vessel movements tracked by Bloomberg.
